1.explanation:
1. We launch Chrome with --disableStorageReset to preserve the site’s service worker.
2. We supply a custom Lighthouse config that only runs the “offline-start-url” audit (which under the hood runs the offline pass via the offline and start-url gatherers).
3. Because of the bug, the audit will report score: 0 (start URL did not load offline) even though a genuine offline fallback UI is served by the service worker.
4. Inspecting this output reproduces the discrepancy between the real offline behavior and what Lighthouse thinks happened.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse against a PWA site that has an offline‐fallback service worker (in this case https://www.bhphotovideo.com/), the offline pass does not actually trigger “offline mode” in Chrome. Instead of seeing the SW’s “You are offline…” fallback UI, Lighthouse still pulls in the live desktop site. Inspecting the network records during the offline pass shows that all requests have fromServiceWorker=false and fromDiskCache=false, which should be impossible when truly offline.
